description: City to budget $241,500 for outdoor washroom project in 2027.

chips.text: Approved
Outdoor Washroom Project costs of $241,500 will be mill rate funded.
Public speakers advocated for more compassionate housing, shelter
Denying disabled persons washroom access may violate Charter rights (Section 15).
Encampment removals disproportionately affect Indigenous, disabled, elderly, women, and children.

speakers.name: Amy-Jo Setka
speakers.summary: Amy-Jo Setka expressed support for continued funding for public washrooms and drop-in services and advocated for improved access to public washrooms and supports for individuals experiencing homelessness.
said: Supports ongoing outdoor washrooms and women's warming/drop-in shelter funding.
Advocates for self-cleaning public washrooms for health and safety.
Denying disabled people washroom access is against charter rights.

speakers.name: Miki Mappin
speakers.summary: Miki Mappin expressed support for ongoing funding for the outdoor washroom project and advocated for expanded shelter, housing and supports for individuals experiencing homelessness.
said: City's encampment eviction was expensive, brutalizing, and ineffective.
Approve annualized funding for outdoor washrooms; they need to be open all year.
Current warm-up shelters are inadequate, unhealthy, dehumanizing, and cruel.

speakers.name: Bonnie Heilman
speakers.summary: Bonnie Heilman spoke in support of increased investment in housing and social supports as a response to homelessness.
said: Building social housing for unhoused people saves taxpayer money.
Redirect police/emergency funding to proactive social housing models.
Housing is a basic human and treaty right for all.

speakers.name: Alexa Volkenburg
speakers.summary: Registered to speak on: Homelessness Encampments
said: Landlords charge high rent for deplorable, inhumane housing conditions.
ORT legislation creates insurmountable barriers for prospective tenants.
Ministry of Social Services provides barriers, not accessible support.

speakers.name: Valerie Senyk
speakers.summary: Registered to speak on: Clearing of the Avenue K Encampment
said: City's forced evacuation of Avenue K encampment was a cruel injustice.
Council should find creative ways to allow encampments to stay.
Housing for homeless is a priority, not a money issue.

speakers.name: Lauren Scruton
speakers.summary: Registered to speak on: Annual Funding for Homelessness Response
said: Encampment cleanup costs are the city's highest annual expense.
Current washroom/shelter funding is inadequate and gender-biased.
City underfunds housing/homelessness while overfunding police.

speakers.name: Chloe Olson
speakers.summary: Registered to speak on: Future path and Plan for handling the Houseless Crisis
said: Police mistreated displaced relatives during encampment clearing.
Removing encampments exacerbates problems by cutting off vital services.
Neglecting point-in-time count leads to incorrect, outdated data.

description: Concerns raised about Crime-Free Multi-Housing Program's effectiveness.
Delegate advocated for tenant reporting, property inspections, and accountability.

chips.text: Approved
Tenants in Crime-Free Multi-Housing properties face safety and maintenance issues.
Public delegate Savannah O'Brien detailed program flaws and tenant safety issues.

speakers.name: Savannah O'Brien
speakers.summary: Registered to speak on: Crime-Free Multi-Housing (CFMH) Program
said: CFMH program is flawed; properties suffer disrepair, security issues.
Managers fail to address issues; police dismiss as civil matters.
Recommends anonymous reporting, proactive inspections, ending program endorsement.
